newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cricket - Davis in good spirits after knee surgery.
newsitem.headline: Cricket - Davis in good spirits after knee surgery.

text.p: WELLINGTON, April 9 - New Zealand cricketer Heath Davis was in good spirits after undergoing surgery on his troublesome knee in Wellington, NZPA reported on Wednesday.
Davis, who had arthroscopic surgery on a cartilage on Tuesday, was at home recuperating today.
"There was a bit of cartilage sticking out and that has been smoothed over," the fast bowler said.
"The bandage will be taken off tomorrow but I am expecting that everything will be okay.
"I am certainly aiming at being ready for the tour to India next month."
Davis was named in the New Zealand side who will play a minimum of three games against Sri Lanka, India and Pakistan, with the possibility of three more if they can make the final.
During his operation, Davis also received treatment for the achilles tendon injury which hampered him during the latter stages of the series against Sri Lanka.

Meanwhile, Davis should be a leading contender for the award of cricket personality of the year when the Shell New Zealand Cricket Awards dinner is held at the Michael Fowler Centre in Wellington tomorrow night.
Last week he was named Wellington's cricketer of the year after firing life back into his international career when selected for the third test against England.
His first five-wicket bag followed in the second test against Sri Lanka and his bowling control was so impressive that he was retained for the one-day series against both England and Sri Lanka.
Along the way he has developed a following among cricket supporters who have revelled in the sight of some genuine firepower in the New Zealand attack.
